y1: When the religious leaders ask, 'By what authority are you doing these things?' Jesus replies with a question about John's baptism. They couldn't answer.
y2: Then comes the parable of the two sons. The younger son who said 'I will go' but didn't represents the outwardly religious leaders, while the older son who said 'I don't want to' but went represents the tax collectors and prostitutes. 'The tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering the kingdom of God ahead of you.'
y3: In the parable in 21:33–46, the owner of the vineyard sends his servants, and finally his son. The tenants kill the son. Jesus foretells His own death and quotes Psalm 118:22: 'The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.'
y5: Those invited to the king's son's wedding banquet made excuses, and even killed the servants. The king says, 'Go to the street corners and invite to the banquet anyone you find.' Both bad and good were gathered at the banquet.
y6: But one man was not wearing wedding clothes. The invitation is free, but one must respond worthily to that invitation. 'For many are called, but few are chosen.'
y7: There is an interpretation that in those days, the host of a banquet provided clothes for the guests. If so, not wearing the clothes was rejecting the host's gift. It means being invited by grace, but refusing to put on grace and insisting on one's own clothes (Isa. 61:10 'garments of salvation').
y9: The Pharisees and Herodians came together. They were usually enemies, but they joined hands to trap Jesus. 'Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar?' If He said 'yes,' He would be a traitor to the people; if He said 'no,' He would be a rebel against Rome.
y10: Jesus has them look at the 'image' and inscription on a denarius. 'Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's.' If the emperor's image is on the coin, what is God's image engraved on? On us ourselves (Gen. 1:27).
y11: In 22:23–33, the Sadducees, who don't believe in the resurrection, test Him with a story of a woman who married seven brothers. Jesus proves the resurrection using Exodus 3:6, saying, 'God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.'
y12: The Foundation of the Entire Law
y13: Rabbis counted the Law as 613 commandments. 'Which is the greatest commandment?' Jesus answers by combining Deuteronomy 6:5 (the Shema) and Leviticus 19:18: loving God and loving your neighbor.
y14: 'All the Law and the Prophets depend on these two commandments.' Like hinges holding a door, the whole Law hangs on these two. Then Jesus asks the final question: 'Whose son is the Christ?' He is the one David called 'Lord,' which is Jesus (Ps. 110:1).
y15: Jesus says the second commandment is 'like' the first. Whether love for God is genuine is shown by love for one's neighbor (1 John 4:20). Conversely, the power to love one's neighbor comes from loving God.
verse: “Jesus said to him, ‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the first and greatest commandment. A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”
prayer: Dear God, thank You for inviting me to the banquet for free and clothing me with the righteousness of Jesus. Let me not just say 'yes' with my words, but obey. Let me give myself, who is Your image, to You, love You with all my heart, soul, and mind, and love my neighbor as myself. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: authority. A key word in the Gospel of Matthew, connected to 7:29, 9:6, and 28:18. Jesus's authority is from heaven. “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth” (28:18).
d1: wedding banquet. The Bible describes the last day as the 'wedding banquet of the Lamb' (Rev. 19:9). It also appears in the parable of the ten virgins in chapter 25. In 9:15, Jesus called Himself the 'bridegroom'.
d2: image. The denarius had the face of Emperor Tiberius and the inscription 'son of god.' God's image is engraved on humans. This is the root of the word 'icon'.
d3: love. It is not just a feeling, but a love that chooses what is best for the other person. The same verb is used for loving enemies in 5:44. “Love is the fulfillment of the law” (Rom. 13:10).
